summary: AE/SE intro call to qualify Equinox Labs' interest in migrating from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated (possibly private). Key priorities: eval parity with OpenAI outputs, latency p95/p99 targets for synchronous chat endpoints, security (SOC2/KMS/VPC), and predictable cost. Customer is interested in a 2-week POC to validate throughput and output parity using their prompt set. Redwood to provide pricing, SOW, security docs, and benchmarking plan.
topics: Current stack and pain points (OpenAI, costs)
Compatibility concerns: vLLM / TGI / tokenization parity
Performance targets and hardware sizing (latency vs throughput)
Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs, SSO
POC scope: eval parity, benchmarks, timeline
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-06 16:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees listed above

Summary (auto): quick intro, qualification, technical deep dive on migration risks, next steps and action items.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, i'll kick us off, we got dan and priya on the line as well. how's everyone doing?
00:06 Speaker 2 (Jared): doing good, thanks. excited to talk through the options here, we've been running on OpenAI endpoints for about 18 months.
00:14 Speaker 3 (Rosa): hi, rosa here from infra, i've got some questions on VPC and audit logs.
00:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): great, quick agenda: understand your current stack/costs, key success criteria, then dan/priya will cover compatibility and perf, then wrap with next steps.
00:28 Speaker 4 (Tom): we mainly use gpt-4 style endpoints for chat, about 5k rps of token generation during peak, costs are creeping and we'd like more predictability.
00:40 Speaker 2 (Jared): also we're seeing occasional output variance across vendor updates; we need eval parity so product UX doesn't regress.
00:48 Speaker 5 (Daniel): yep, thanks. from the se side, our main focus is model parity and runtime compatibility. two common migration paths: hosted (same API), dedicated (reserved GPU pool) and private (VPC/on-prem). you mentioned dedicated might be a fit?
01:02 Speaker 3 (Rosa): yes, dedicated for isolation and cost predictability. we also need KMS integration and audit trails.
01:08 Speaker 6 (Priya): for eval parity, we typically run the customer's prompt set through both source provider and our runtime to measure delta on metrics: exact match, BLEU-ish scores, hallucination rates and latency. we can do that during a 2-week pilot.
01:28 Speaker 2 (Jared): quick question on vLLM and TGI - we run an internal stack sometimes with vLLM for cost reasons. will that map cleanly to Redwood?
01:36 Speaker 5 (Daniel): good question. Redwood's runtime supports model weights commonly used by OpenAI-equivalent families; we support the same tokenizers and provide quantization guidance. if you're running vLLM/TGI as a local serving layer, the main migration risk is inference kernel differences and tokenization flags. we can run a parity test that exercises both setups. sometimes folks see slight temperature/response distribution shifts, especially with quantized weights.
02:05 Speaker 4 (Tom): hardware sizing - what are we looking at for 5k rps? we saw some docs that suggested autoscaling with multiple A100s or H100s.
02:14 Speaker 5 (Daniel): depends on sequence length and duped requests. ballpark: for synchronous chat with avg seq 512 tokens and 5k concurrent requests (not rps, you said rps earlier - clarifying), if you mean 5k tokens per second we size much lower; if 5k concurrent users, that's different. can you confirm?
02:30 Speaker 4 (Tom): sorry, we meant peak concurrent requests ~200, aggregate token throughput ~5k tokens/sec.
02:36 Speaker 5 (Daniel): perfect - for that profile a small dedicated cluster (2-4 A100 GPUs with batching + prefix cache) typically meets p95 latency targets around 200-250ms on chat completions. p99 depends on tail and can be higher; we use prefix KV cache and continuous batching to keep costs down.
02:58 Speaker 3 (Rosa): on security, we need SSO/SAML, RBAC, and customer-managed KMS. any compliance docs?
03:06 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes we have SOC2 and ISO artifacts, plus documentation on KMS integration and audit logs. we'll share the bundle.
03:12 Speaker 2 (Jared): eval parity - how do you measure differences? we can't afford regressions in user-facing flows.
03:18 Speaker 6 (Priya): we run side-by-side A/B with the same prompts, compute similarity metrics, and then manual spot checks for correctness/hallucination. we can also tune sampling/temp, top_k and provide model/quantization recommendations. sometimes the simple thing is pinning to a particular model version to reduce drift.
03:36 Speaker 2 (Jared): if we pin a model, will Redwood keep that binary on Dedicated?
03:40 Speaker 5 (Daniel): yes, dedicated gives you pinned model versions and ability to freeze rollouts. autoscaler and fallback policies are configurable.
03:46 Speaker 4 (Tom): latency vs cost tradeoffs - can we get suggested batch sizes and quant profiles?
03:52 Speaker 6 (Priya): absolutely, we'll run microbenchmarks with your prompts and give you a recommended config (batch sizes, quantization profile, kernel selection). note: quantization sometimes changes output slightly, we'll measure that during pilot.
04:08 Speaker 3 (Asha): security again - do you support bringing your own HSM?
04:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments; Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS in the cloud region.
04:20 Speaker 2 (Jared): what's the pilot scope and success criteria we should set?
04:24 Speaker 5 (Daniel): typical pilot: 2 weeks where we run your prompt set and live traffic mirror for a subset of traffic. goals: demonstrate parity thresholds (we can agree on metrics), meet p95/p99 latency SLOs for a canary route, and produce cost estimates and hardware sizing.
04:40 Speaker 4 (Tom): that sounds good. timeline - we want to move quickly; can you send pricing and SOW?
04:44 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes i'll send Dedicated pricing deck and sample SOW by end of week (i'll target 3/10). dan will kick off the benchmark sheet and pilot scheduling.
04:52 Speaker 2 (Jared): any hidden limitations coming from model format differences? we do some custom tokenizers for certain inputs.
04:58 Speaker 6 (Priya): we'll need a sample of your tokenizer config and prompt set; if you have custom tokenizers we can run a tokenization parity test. often it's minor flag changes. we also check for differences in newline handling and special tokens which can change outputs.
05:12 Speaker 3 (Rosa): on network/comms: can Dedicated be deployed in our VPC? we need private connectivity and control plane separation.
05:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): Dedicated supports private peering, VPC connectors and a private control plane option for enterprise. for air-gapped on-prem we have Redwood Private options but that takes a longer lead time.
05:30 Speaker 2 (Jared): pricing question - do you do committed monthly for Dedicated?
05:34 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, reserved capacity contracts with monthly/annual commits. we'll include a delta comparison vs your current OpenAI monthly spend and expected TCO under various traffic shapes.
05:44 Speaker 4 (Tom): legal / procurement - do you have standard security addendums?
05:48 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, we have sample DPA and standard addenda, and we'll share compliance artifacts.
05:54 Speaker 5 (Daniel): technical note - if you're running vLLM locally today, some teams use it for cheaper batch workloads. for real-time chat we recommend our optimized runtime because of KV caching and kernel selection which reduces p99. we'll show microbenchmarks during the pilot.
06:14 Speaker 2 (Jared): ok would like to see a sample benchmark and a playbook for how you tune quant profiles.
06:20 Speaker 6 (Priya): we'll include that. we'll also provide a short runbook for rollouts and fallback policies (e.g., route to hosted as fallback).
06:30 Speaker 3 (Asha): final question - data residency, we need EU-only processing for a subset of traffic. can you regionally route?
06:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, smart routing by region is supported. you can pin routes to EU clusters and we provide audit logs showing data flow.
06:44 Speaker 2 (Jared): great. sounds like next steps are pricing, SOW, SOC2 docs, pilot plan and benchmark sheet.
06:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): yep will do. thanks everyone for the time.
06:54 Speaker 4 (Tom): thanks, talk soon.

Post-call notes: Redwood to run parity eval with Equinox prompt set, target go/no-go within 2 weeks of pilot start. Attachments referenced: Dedicated pricing deck (link to share), SOC2 bundle (link to share), benchmark spreadsheet (to be created).
